subject: INITIALIZE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB416.md LANDED. identifier-1's class is screened at the one place it is resolved: BindInitializeTarget asks IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOfPlace -- the ONE §8.5.2.1 Table-2 classifier -- and reports COBOL2030 when the answer is class INDEX. Of the nine classes Table 2 lists, SR1's list admits eight and excludes exactly that one (§8.5.2.8: 'an elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage index'), so the whole rule is one predicate. It is written as its OWN screen and not as a widening of §14.9.20.4 GR5a1's receiver exclusion, because the two rules answer different questions about different items: GR5a1 excludes an index item CONTAINED IN identifier-1 and must keep its SILENCE, which the positive golden pins (G carries a subordinate USAGE INDEX item and INITIALIZE G skips it without a word while initializing its siblings). The eight admitted classes are exercised by the same golden -- an alphanumeric group, an elementary numeric item, an elementary alphabetic item -- and a strongly-typed group and a USAGE POINTER target were probed directly. Version-invariant: SR1 and its class list are COBOL-85, and the negative rejects at all four editions.
